title: Wishes and Preferences
description: Express regret, preferences and complaints with wish / if only + past simple and past perfect, wish + would, would rather, and it's (high) time + past simple. Vocabulary: lifestyle, habits and complaints.
objectives: Express regrets about the present and the past with wish and if only
Complain about annoying habits with wish + would
State preferences with would rather and would prefer
Say that something should happen now with it's (high) time + past simple, and make polite complaints

lessons.title: Wish and If Only: Present and Past Regrets
lessons.summary: Mengungkapkan penyesalan tentang masa kini (wish + past simple) dan masa lalu (wish + past perfect).
objectives: Review wish + past simple for present situations
Use wish / if only + past perfect for past regrets
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Wishes go 'one step back' in time
When we wish for something **unreal**, the verb moves one step into the past, just like in conditionals.

| Time of the wish | Structure | Example | Reality |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| present | wish + **past simple** | *I wish I **had** more time.* | I don't have enough time. |
| present (be) | wish + **were/was** | *I wish I **were** taller.* | I'm not tall. |
| present ability | wish + **could** | *I wish I **could** swim.* | I can't swim. |
| past | wish + **past perfect** | *I wish I **had studied** harder.* | I didn't study hard. |

### Past regrets: wish + past perfect
This is the key B2 structure. It expresses **regret** about something that did or didn't happen:
- *I wish I **had gone** to the party.* (I didn't go.)
- *I wish I **hadn't sold** my old guitar.* (I sold it.)
- *She wishes she **had taken** the job in Singapore.*

### if only
*If only* means the same as *I wish* but is **stronger and more emotional**:
- ***If only** I **had listened** to my parents!*
- ***If only** we **hadn't missed** the flight.*

### Never use would have after wish
- ✗ *I wish I would have known.*
- ✓ *I wish I **had known**.*

### Connection with the third conditional
Wishes about the past use the same tense as the if-clause of the third conditional:
- *I wish I had saved money.* → *If I had saved money, I would have bought a house.*

### was or were?
After *wish*, *were* is used for all persons in formal English; *was* is common in informal speech: *I wish I **were/was** on holiday.*

> **Catatan:** *Andai saja / seandainya* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak mengubah bentuk kata kerja. Dalam bahasa Inggris, untuk masa kini pakai **past simple** (*I wish I knew*), untuk masa lalu pakai **past perfect** (*I wish I had known*). Jangan pakai *would have* setelah *wish*.

lessons.title: Wish + Would: Annoying Habits
lessons.summary: Mengeluhkan kebiasaan orang lain atau situasi yang ingin diubah dengan wish + would.
objectives: Use wish + would to complain about other people's habits
Use wish + would for situations we want to change (I wish it would stop raining)
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### wish + would: wanting someone or something to change
We use **wish + someone/something + would + infinitive** when we are **annoyed** or **impatient** and want a change in the future:
- *I wish my neighbour **would stop** playing loud music at night.*
- *I wish you **wouldn't interrupt** me all the time.*
- *I wish it **would stop** raining!*

It is often a **complaint** or a polite criticism.

### The subject must be different
We don't normally say *I wish I would...*, because we can control our own actions. Use *could* or the past simple instead:
- ✗ *I wish I would be taller.* → ✓ *I wish I **were** taller.*
- ✗ *I wish I would have a car.* → ✓ *I wish I **had** a car.*
- ✗ *I wish I would go out more.* → ✓ *I wish I **could** go out more.*

### Only for actions, not states
*Would* is used with actions (*stop, call, listen, tidy*), not states:
- ✗ *I wish you would be here.* → ✓ *I wish you **were** here.*
- ✗ *I wish he would have more money.* → ✓ *I wish he **had** more money.*

### Summary of wish structures
| Structure | Use | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| wish + past simple | unreal present state | *I wish I **had** my own room.* |
| wish + could | ability / possibility | *I wish I **could** drive.* |
| wish + past perfect | past regret | *I wish I **hadn't lent** him my jacket.* |
| wish + would | annoying habit / desired change | *I wish he **wouldn't borrow** my clothes.* |

### Tone
*I wish you would...* can sound quite critical. To be more polite, use: *Would you mind...?* or *Could you possibly...?*

> **Catatan:** *I wish you would ...* ≈ *Saya harap kamu mau ...* (dengan nada kesal). Contoh: *Saya harap tetangga berhenti menyetel musik keras* → *I wish my neighbour would stop playing loud music.* Jangan pakai *I wish I would ...*.

lessons.title: Would Rather and Would Prefer
lessons.summary: Mengungkapkan preferensi dengan would rather (+ infinitive / + subjek + past simple) dan would prefer.
objectives: Use would rather + infinitive (than) for your own preferences
Use would rather + subject + past simple for other people's actions
Compare would rather, would prefer and prefer
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### would rather + infinitive (same subject)
Use it to talk about **your own** preferences. It is followed by the **bare infinitive** (no *to*):
- *I'd rather **stay** at home tonight.*
- *I'd rather **walk** than **take** the bus.* (than + bare infinitive)
- *I'd rather **not** talk about it.* (negative: rather not)
- *Would you rather **have** tea or coffee?*

### would rather + subject + past simple (different subject)
When you want **another person** to do something, use the **past simple** (with present or future meaning):
- *I'd rather **you didn't smoke** in here.*
- *I'd rather **we stayed** in tonight, if you don't mind.*
- *My parents would rather **I studied** medicine.*

This is a polite way to make a request or show disapproval.

### Comparing preference structures
| Structure | Followed by | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| would rather | bare infinitive (+ than + bare infinitive) | *I'd rather **walk** than **drive**.* |
| would rather + subject | past simple | *I'd rather **you drove**.* |
| would prefer | to-infinitive (+ rather than + bare infinitive) | *I'd prefer **to walk** rather than **drive**.* |
| would prefer + object | to-infinitive | *I'd prefer **you to drive**.* |
| prefer (general) | -ing **to** -ing / noun **to** noun | *I prefer **walking to driving**.* |

### Contractions
*I'd rather* = *I would rather*; *I'd prefer* = *I would prefer*. Don't write *I rather*.

### Common errors
- ✗ *I'd rather to stay.* → ✓ *I'd rather stay.*
- ✗ *I'd rather you don't tell anyone.* → ✓ *I'd rather you didn't tell anyone.*
- ✗ *I prefer coffee than tea.* → ✓ *I prefer coffee **to** tea.*

> **Catatan:** *I'd rather* = *saya lebih suka / saya lebih memilih*. Untuk diri sendiri: *I'd rather + V1*. Untuk orang lain: *I'd rather you + V2 (past simple)* — artinya *saya lebih suka kalau kamu ...*. Contoh: *Saya lebih suka kamu tidak merokok di sini* = *I'd rather you didn't smoke here.*

lessons.title: It's (High) Time + Past Simple
lessons.summary: Mengatakan bahwa sesuatu seharusnya sudah dilakukan dengan it's time / it's high time / it's about time.
objectives: Use it's time + to-infinitive for neutral statements
Use it's (high/about) time + subject + past simple to criticise or urge
Compare it's time with had better and should
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Two patterns
| Pattern | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| it's time + **to-infinitive** | neutral: the right moment has come | *It's time **to start** the meeting.* |
| it's time + (for + person) + **to-infinitive** | neutral, with a person | *It's time **for us to go**.* |
| it's time + subject + **past simple** | it should happen now (maybe it's a little late) | *It's time **we went** home.* |
| it's **high time / about time** + subject + **past simple** | criticism: it should have happened already | *It's high time **you found** a job.* |

### Past simple, present meaning
As with *wish* and *would rather*, the past simple here refers to the **present/future**. It shows the action hasn't happened yet:
- *It's late. **It's time we left**.* (We haven't left yet; we should leave now.)
- ✗ *It's time we leave.*

### high time / about time
Adding *high* or *about* makes the sentence stronger and more critical:
- *It's **about time** the council **repaired** this road!* (It should have happened long ago.)
- *It's **high time** you **had** your hair cut.* (causative from Unit 4!)

### Related structures for advice and urgency
| Structure | Strength | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| You should... | advice | *You should see a doctor.* |
| You'd better... | strong advice / warning | *You'd better hurry, or you'll miss the train.* |
| It's time you... | it should happen now | *It's time you saw a doctor.* |
| It's high time you... | criticism: it's late | *It's high time you saw a doctor.* |

Note: *had better* + bare infinitive: *You'd better **not be** late* (NOT *had better to*).

### Negatives
We usually avoid negatives after *it's time*. Instead of *It's time you didn't...*, say *It's time you stopped...*.

> **Catatan:** *It's time we went home* = *Sudah waktunya kita pulang*. Walaupun memakai past simple (*went*), maknanya **sekarang**. *It's high time / about time* = *sudah seharusnya dari dulu* (ada nada kritik).

mistakes.wrong: It's high time the council repairs this road.

sections.summary: **It's time + to-infinitive** is neutral; **It's (high/about) time + subject + past simple** means something should happen now (and maybe should have happened earlier). The past simple has present meaning. Compare with *should* and *had better*. *Ringkasan: It's time we went = sudah waktunya kita pergi.*

lessons.title: Vocabulary: Lifestyle, Habits and Complaints
lessons.summary: Kosakata tentang gaya hidup, kebiasaan, dan cara menyampaikan keluhan dengan sopan.
objectives: Use phrasal verbs and expressions for habits (cut down on, give up, get into the habit of)
Talk about annoyance (put up with, get on someone's nerves, fed up with)
Make polite spoken and written complaints
lessons.completionCriteria: Complete the speaking task and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Selesaikan tugas berbicara dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Habits and lifestyle
| Expression | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cut down on | reduce | I'm trying to **cut down on** sugar. |
| give up | stop completely | He **gave up** smoking last year. |
| get into the habit of + -ing | start doing regularly | I've **got into the habit of** walking to work. |
| break a habit | stop a habit | It's hard to **break** a bad **habit**. |
| sedentary | involving a lot of sitting | a **sedentary** lifestyle |
| work out | exercise | She **works out** three times a week. |

### Annoyance
| Expression | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| put up with | tolerate | I can't **put up with** the noise any longer. |
| get on sb's nerves | annoy sb | His whistling **gets on my nerves**. |
| be fed up with | be bored/annoyed with | I'm **fed up with** waiting. |
| drive sb crazy/mad | annoy sb very much | The traffic **drives me crazy**. |

Remember the prepositions: *fed up **with**, put up **with**, cut down **on***. After prepositions, use **-ing**.

### Making a polite complaint (spoken)
1. **Get attention politely**: *Excuse me, I'm afraid there's a problem with...*
2. **Explain**: *The air conditioning in my room isn't working.*
3. **Ask for action**: *Could you possibly send someone to look at it?* / *I'd rather you moved me to another room.*
4. **Stay calm**: avoid *You must...!* or *This is terrible!*

### Making a formal complaint (written)
| Part | Useful language |
| --- | --- |
| Reason for writing | *I am writing to complain about...* |
| Details | *On 3 May, I bought... Unfortunately, ...* |
| Effect | *As a result, I was unable to...* |
| Request | *I would be grateful if you could arrange a refund / replacement.* |
| Closing | *I look forward to hearing from you.* |

Key nouns: **refund** (money back), **replacement** (a new item), **compensation** (money for a loss or problem), **faulty** (not working correctly).

### Using this unit's grammar
*I wish the hotel **had told** us about the building work. It's **high time** they **replaced** the lift. I'd **rather** you **didn't** charge us for the extra night.*

> **Catatan:** Dalam budaya berbahasa Inggris, keluhan yang efektif biasanya **sopan dan spesifik**. Gunakan *I'm afraid...*, *Could you possibly...?*, *I would be grateful if...*. *Refund* = pengembalian uang; *compensation* = ganti rugi; *faulty* = rusak/cacat.

examples.en: I'm trying to cut down on coffee; I only have one cup a day now.

vocabulary.example: Doctors advise us to cut down on salt.
I won't put up with this noise.
I'm fed up with the delays.
Office workers often have a sedentary lifestyle.
I asked for a full refund.
The charger I bought was faulty.

grammar.pattern: be fed up with / put up with / cut down on + noun / -ing
grammar.example: I'm fed up with cooking every night.

grammar.pattern: I would be grateful if you could + infinitive
grammar.example: I would be grateful if you could reply soon.
I'm afraid the order is incomplete.
grammar.note: Polite way to introduce a problem.

mistakes.wrong: I'm fed up of to wait.
I can't put up this noise.
mistakes.right: I can't put up with this noise.
mistakes.why: The phrasal verb is put up with (three parts).

mistakes.wrong: I want that you give me my money back now.
mistakes.right: I would be grateful if you could give me a refund.
mistakes.why: Want that is incorrect, and the polite form is more effective in a complaint.

sections.summary: Talk about habits with **cut down on, give up, get into the habit of, break a habit, sedentary**; about annoyance with **put up with, get on my nerves, fed up with**; and complain politely with **I'm afraid..., Could you possibly...?, I would be grateful if you could...**, asking for a **refund, replacement** or **compensation**. *Ringkasan: keluhan yang sopan dan jelas lebih efektif.*

questions.instructions: Hint: she hasn't stopped completely; she's reducing.
questions.context: I've decided to ___ sugar: I now have one spoon in my coffee instead of three.
options: cut down on
give up
put up with
get on
questions.explanation: Reducing (not stopping completely) → **cut down on**. *Give up* = stop completely; *put up with* = tolerate.

questions.prompt: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.right: involving a lot of sitting and little exercise

questions.explanation: These expressions are common when talking about lifestyle changes and everyday annoyances.

dialogue.speaker: Receptionist
dialogue.text: Good evening. How can I help you?

options: I'm afraid there's a problem with my room: the air conditioning isn't working.
Your hotel is terrible and I want my money now!
I wish you would to fix the air conditioning.
It's high time you repair the air conditioning.
questions.explanation: **I'm afraid there's a problem with...** is polite and clear. Option 2 is rude, and options 3 and 4 contain grammar errors (*would to*, *repair* instead of *repaired*).

questions.prompt: Role-play: you ordered a vegetarian meal in a restaurant, but it arrived with meat, and you have been waiting 45 minutes. Complain politely to the manager and ask for a solution.
questions.sampleAnswer: Excuse me, I'm afraid there's a problem with my order. I asked for the vegetarian curry, but this one has chicken in it, and we've been waiting for about 45 minutes. I wish the waiter had checked the order before bringing it. Could you possibly ask the kitchen to prepare the correct dish quickly? And I'd rather you didn't charge us for the drinks, if that's possible. Thank you.
questions.explanation: A good complaint is polite, explains the problem clearly and asks for a specific solution.

questions.prompt: Complete the text with words from the bank.
questions.text: I'm ___ up with my flatmate. He never cleans, and his loud music really gets on my ___. I don't know how much longer I can put up ___ it.
answers: fed
nerves
with
questions.explanation: **fed up with** (muak), **get on my nerves** (membuat kesal), **put up with** (tahan dengan).

questions.prompt: Put the fragments in order to make a sentence for a formal complaint email.
fragments: I am writing to complain about
that I bought from your store last week,
and I would be grateful if you could
questions.explanation: Reason for writing → the problem → details → polite formal request.

questions.prompt: Which is the most appropriate way to end a formal complaint email?
options: I look forward to hearing from you.
Write back soon, OK?
See you later!
Fix it now.
questions.explanation: **I look forward to hearing from you** is the standard formal closing. The others are too informal or rude.

unitTestQuestions.context: I wish I ___ to your advice last year.
options: had listened
listened
would listen
have listened
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Last year* → past regret → **wish + past perfect**: *had listened*.

unitTestQuestions.sentence: My flatmate keeps leaving dirty dishes in the sink. It's so annoying!
unitTestQuestions.cue: Begin with: I wish my flatmate ...
answers: I wish my flatmate wouldn't leave dirty dishes in the sink.
I wish my flatmate would not leave dirty dishes in the sink.
I wish my flatmate would stop leaving dirty dishes in the sink.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Complete with the correct form. Use the words in brackets.
unitTestQuestions.text: I'd rather you ___ (not / call) me after 10 p.m.
answers: didn't call
did not call
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Different subject after *would rather* → **past simple**: *I'd rather you didn't call me.*
After *it's high time + subject*, use the **past simple**: *the government did something*.

unitTestQuestions.text: If only I ___ the answer! Then I could help you right now.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: A wish about the present (*right now*) → **past simple**: *If only I knew the answer!*

unitTestQuestions.source: Saya lebih suka tinggal di rumah daripada pergi ke mal.
answers: I'd rather stay at home than go to the mall.
I would rather stay at home than go to the mall.
I'd rather stay home than go to the mall.
I would rather stay home than go to the mall.
I prefer staying at home to going to the mall.
I prefer to stay at home rather than go to the mall.
I'd prefer to stay at home rather than go to the mall.
I would prefer to stay at home rather than go to the mall.
I'd rather stay at home than go to the shopping centre.
I'd rather stay at home than go to the shopping mall.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Lebih suka ... daripada ...* = **would rather + verb + than + verb**, or **prefer -ing to -ing**.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: What does the phrase in bold mean?
unitTestQuestions.context: I've lived next to the building site for a year, but I can't **put up with** the noise any longer.
options: tolerate
make louder
record
complain about in writing
unitTestQuestions.explanation: **Put up with** = tolerate something unpleasant (tahan dengan).
